text: A few miles from Boston, in Massachusetts, a narrow inlet winds far into the country and ends in a thickly wooded swamp. <break time="0.8s" /> According to an old story, Kidd the pirate buried a great treasure under one of the giant oaks that stand beside this inlet. <break time="0.8s" /> Kidd never returned for it, because soon afterward he was arrested in Boston, sent to England, and executed as a pirate. <break time="0.8s" /> People also say that the devil himself watched over the hiding of the gold and has guarded it closely ever since. <break time="0.8s" /> About the year 1727, there lived near this place a mean, greedy man named Tom Walker, who had a wife as miserly as himself. <break time="0.8s" /> So miserly were the two that they even tried to cheat each other, and whatever the wife could get her hands on, she hid away. <break time="0.8s" /> They quarreled so loudly and so often that a lonely traveler passing their house would stop to listen and then hurry on his way. <break time="0.8s" /> Their house stood alone in a bare field, and like its owners, it had a hungry, half starved look about it. <break time="0.8s" /> A miserable horse, its ribs showing like the bars of a grill, wandered about the field in search of something to eat.
